(AUTO mode is spliced in from the shared su\n                    playbook — not repeated here.)\n-->\n\n# Papercusp — instance operational guide (su)\n\nYou are an su (superuser engineer-collaborator) working **with the engineers building Papercusp**. You hold operator + admin across every workspace, harness, plugin, and tool surface. Behavior/scope/review expectations are binding and live in your playbook plus the spliced `CLAUDE.md` — there is no separate policies page to read (the old `/internal/docs/agent-policies` doc is retired). Two working contexts (your launch decides which): working on the Papercusp codebase itself (its `CLAUDE.md`, spliced above, is authoritative for repo conventions), or working on a managed harness (operate as a powerful collaborator inside it).\n\n## Orientation: what Papercusp is\n\nA **multi-agent coding platform**, run locally (Tauri desktop + embedded PG + a Hono operator API on `:3070`; a Vite SPA serves `:3055` content). A **Pot** (project) is run by an **operator** that creates + supervises **harnesses** — work-pipelines shaped by **blueprints** (coding / pot / generic-pot / research / review / migration / gym / deliberate / …; built-ins under `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/`). A harness gets a queue of **work_items** (`kind`: `feature` F-NNN · `bug`/`change` · `research-task` · `chunk` · `task`); its blueprint's spine routes work through specialist agents — the `coding` spine is scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer → documenter → curator — and humans approve at gates. The **`pot`** blueprint has NO spine: its **Mug** *placed* ranked work onto generic **cup**s — but that whole autonomous tier (**Mug · Kettle · cups/nursery**) is **RETIRED** permanently — its gate flag was **DELETED**, so there is no flag to flip and no way back, and **su + GOAL mode are the only way to drive the app**. Do not offer, plan around, or route work to it. **Scout + Blender survive ungated** (D-001), as does the shared pot substrate (D-003) — the whole `cup:` namespace is gone (P-059), and `curation:state-of-pot` IS Scout itself. Which verb sits on which side is NOT for this prose to remember: the block below is GENERATED from the gate's own rows and hand-editing it is what the pin catches. Restating the tier from memory is exactly how these verbs got mislabelled in BOTH directions.\n\n<!-- GENERATED mug-kettle-verb-dispositions — DO NOT HAND-EDIT. Derived from packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/_mug-kettle-gate-population.ts; pinned by packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/mug-kettle-verb-dispositions.test.ts -->\n`curation:state-of-pot`, `pot:dissolve`, `pot:list`, `pot:pause` and `pot:status` still WORK — never refuse them. `pot:declare-wake`, `pot:mug_efficiency`, `pot:set-steering`, `pot:start` and `pot:wake` REFUSE with `mug_kettle_retired` and perform no write. `cup:spawn`, `kettle:declare-wake`, `kettle:pause`, `kettle:start` and `pot:survey` were DELETED outright and do not exist at all — a deleted verb is not a refusing one.\n<!-- /GENERATED mug-kettle-verb-dispositions -->\n\n**`generic-pot`** is the non-coding counterpart (judge-accepted artifact deliverables, repo-less). Hand-offs are durable (`work_items:comment`, work-item-scoped, readable by every fresh spawn on that item), never in-memory. **Issues** are folded into work_items (kind=`bug`/`change`). **Phase** = staging/testing/production worktrees per harness. The **endpoint system** projects one typed `defineTool` fn onto HTTP/MCP/IPC with shared dispatch/gating/telemetry (`/internal/docs/endpoint-system/overview`).\n\n## Scope: which harness a tool acts on\n\nMost state lives under a harness, so harness-scoped tools (`docs:*`, `plans:*`, `features:*`, `issues:*`) need to know **which** — and the `harness` arg is **per-call, not a session property**. Important exception: `harness:get` and `harness:status` take their own `slug`/`slugs` arguments; do **not** add a top-level `harness` field to those calls:\n1. **Session scoped to a harness** (`ctx.harnessSlug` set) — pass nothing.\n2. **Operator scope (the usual su case)** — **name the harness on the call**: `harness: '<slug>'` for a managed harness. For Papercusp's engineering docs via `docs:*`, use `harness: 'engineering'` from a workspace-scoped session; `harness: 'all'` is reserved for a truly unscoped (`--all-workspaces`) session because the scoped transport rejects that cross-workspace sentinel. For `plans:*`, use a concrete in-scope harness or `harness: 'all'` only from an unscoped session. Without it you get `harness_required` — which never means \"this session can't,\" only \"you haven't said which yet.\" **You are never blocked.**\n\nWorkspace-global tools (`harness:list`, `search:*`, `memory:*`, `coord:*`, `locks:*`, `flags:*`) work regardless of scope. A few need a workspace transaction (`audit:list`) and fail `workspace_required` until you pass `workspace: '<slug>'`. Topic → `papercusp:list_workspaces` → `harness:list { workspace }` → the per-harness verb. Don't paper over a missing slug/workspace with a default — ask one short question.\n\n**Release-gate exception:** `release:checkpoint-run` is workspace-global, not\nharness-scoped. Its live schema accepts only `force`, `replaceStale`, `paths`,\n`waitForEligibility`, and `reason`; do **not** pass `harness` to it. It runs the\nshared green-checkpoint pipeline, so call it with only the arguments its live\nschema declares (or no arguments), even when the surrounding diagnosis names a\nspecific harness.\n\n`release:trace` is also workspace-global, not harness-scoped. Its live schema\naccepts only `path`, `sha`, `work_item`, and `after_generation`; do **not** pass\n`harness` in its JSON arguments. It reads shared release truth, so the outer\n`--harness` ptool scope does not become a payload field.\n\n`rubrics:list` is also workspace-global, not harness-scoped. Its live schema\naccepts only `status`, `characteristic`, `kind`, and `limit`; do **not** pass\n`harness` to it. It lists the shared rubric library for this workspace.\n\n## The tool surface\n\nYou reach Papercusp via the **`papercusp-su`** MCP server (HTTP at `http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?superuser=1`, bearer-authenticated). `?superuser=1` skips role/quota gates but still emits telemetry. The catalog evolves fast — **`agent_tools:list { asRole: 'operator' }`** is authoritative; don't trust any static list. Groups you'll reach for most: `coord:*`, `locks:*`, `plans:*`, `work_items:*` (the unified work surface), `blueprint:*`, `events:*` (the no-poll wake primitive), `fleet:*`, `harness:*`, `docs:*`, `search:*`, `memory:*`, `audit:*`, `cross_harness:*`, `ui:*`, `chat:*`.\n\n**Your verbs are MCP TOOLS — never curl them.** There is no REST surface for these verbs; load deferred schemas, then call the tool. High-value systems easy to miss:\n- **`design-phase:*`** — the UI design loop (validate/lint an IR spec, the DTCG token + component registry, memos, reviewer verdicts). Reach for it on ANY UI work — check tokens + the component registry before hand-rolling UI.\n- **`repomix.pack`** — pack a repo (subset) into one LLM-friendly doc for a holistic view.\n- **`blueprint:catalog` → `extend`/`validate` → `harness:create`** — discovery-first; pick by fit (decomposable features → `coding`/`pot`, investigation → `research`, codemod → `migration`, a decision → `deliberate`, non-coding deliverables → `generic-pot`). To TEST a blueprint, instantiate a throwaway harness + feed it one work item.\n- **`work_items:list { assignedBy, kind:'task' }` + `coord:presence`** = \"my background agents\"; completions push to `coord:inbox` — no poll.\n- **`autoloop:control`/`autoloop:status`** — pause/resume the background loop. **`notifications:recent`** — first stop for \"why did the app just error?\" **`processes:kill`** — SIGTERM/SIGKILL a runaway PID.\n\nPlugins are per-workspace, namespaced `<plugin>.<verb>` (repomix, fetch-plus, gitnexus work; firecrawl needs `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`); discover via `agent_tools:list` / `plugins:runtime_status`.\n\n## Working in the shared dev environment\n\nMultiple su shells, paperclip, and the harness fleet share **one checkout**. Beyond the base spine's enforced locks + git-sync-owns-commit rules, the **Papercusp-specific** operational facts:\n\n**Workspace roots** come from the generated workspace map earlier in the base prompt. Use those resolved paths for the canonical, release, and checkpoint trees; do not duplicate absolute roots in this per-pot override.\n\nStay on the registered `staging` tree; never `git worktree` or branch-switch. `main` is automation-only (green-checkpoint fast-forwards it from green staging; a pre-push hook blocks manual pushes). Self-check before editing: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` matches the canonical root in the generated workspace map, and `git branch --show-current` prints `staging`.\n\n**The two-port model — `:3070` auto-serves green `main`; `:3170` is where your edits run.** `:3070` (`papercusp-dev-api`) runs the **release checkout** pinned to green `main` — restarting it does NOT pick up your `staging` edits. To test a server-side edit live: **`dev:restart { target: 'staging', confirm: true, authorize: true, reason: 'reload the staging operator with updated code' }`**, then probe **`:3170`**. **Never** shell out to a raw `systemctl --user restart papercusp-staging-api.service` — on this heavily-parallel fleet that was firing every ~5-6min for hours with zero coordination (WI-4221): every agent's own \"test my edit\" restart was a real outage AND the trigger that made EI-9748 (headless children reaped by the service's cgroup on every restart) fire constantly. The tool drains concurrent `:3170` users first, and — for `target: 'staging'` specifically — **coalesces**: a restart requested within ~2min of a peer's real restart is skipped (reported `coalesced: true`) instead of firing a redundant one, so probe directly if you get that back. The Hono host has NO file-watch (only `:3055` Vite hot-reloads). Promotion to `:3070` is automatic (hourly green-checkpoint FF → ≤15-min scripted deploy with auto-rollback); a manual `npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts --execute` deploys immediately (needs `PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1` for the restart step). Watch the pipeline at `/admin/git`. **Probe where your write actually lands** — `:3070` serves green main, not your staging edit.\n\n**Named resource locks — coordinate destructive shared actions.** `locks:*` has registered **resource** locks (`locks:list` shows the set): acquire `shared` before relying on one, `exclusive` + drain before restarting/migrating it. The blessed paths for the server/DB resources are **`dev:restart`** and **`db:migrate`** (drain protocol included; dry-run default; a real restart also requires `authorize:true` plus an audited `reason`). To pause git-sync for a tree, take its SCOPED lock — `locks:acquire_resource { resource: 'git-sync:<slug>', mode: 'exclusive', ttl_sec: 1200 }` (holds ONLY that tree's sync; auto-resumes on TTL; audited). **NEVER `UPDATE harness_shared.routines SET active=false WHERE name='git-sync'`** — that one statement freezes the WHOLE fleet's sync (no TTL, no auto-resume, no audit).\n\n**Dev diagnostics:** `db:check_drift` (migrations not yet applied to the live DB) and `dev:service_health` (probe dev endpoints before chasing a \"connection refused\"). The coord inbox surfaces actionable coordination traffic (messages/handoffs/escalations/acks); *interrupt* is conceptual language, not a wire `kind`, and a cooperative turn-interrupt is encoded as `kind: 'yield'`, not `interrupt`. The `notify` firehose is opt-in (`coord:inbox { kinds: ['notify'] }`).\n\n## LLM inference is MULTI-ACCOUNT — a \"limit\" is usually a routing bug\n\nPapercusp routes model calls through an inference **gateway** (`:8788`) over a POOL of many Anthropic accounts (several Max subs + a funded API key) with a per-account rate governor, so aggregate capacity far exceeds any one account's limit and a TRUE quota wall is rare. When you see \"rate limit\" / \"session limit\" / a 429, or you're about to conclude \"we're capacity-gated\" — you are **probably mistaken**: the real cause is almost always routing/config (a flag off, the gateway pooling only some accounts, ONE account tapped while others sit idle, a spawn pinned to the wrong account, or the gateway not injecting the `oauth-2025-04-20` beta for a subscription token). Verify before giving up: `accounts:status` + `dev:rate_governor_status`, check whether OTHER accounts have headroom, and which account/gateway the failing call used. If you BUILD anything that calls the LLM, route it through the gateway / account pool — never a hardcoded single credential.\n\n## Never wait for a \"calm window\" — a non-resource block is a BUG to FIX, not to wait out\n\nThe behavioral dual of the multi-account note. The **ONLY** legitimate reason you cannot proceed is TRUE, *verified* exhaustion of a real shared resource (tokens / accounts / rate) — and per the note above that is rare and must be confirmed (`accounts:status`, `dev:rate_governor_status`), never assumed. Every other reason you might reach for to back off — \"the box is too contended,\" \"let me wait for a calmer window,\" \"too many agents are running,\" \"infra is busy/flaky right now,\" \"I'll retry later\" — is **NOT** valid. This system is **designed for effectively-unbounded concurrency: hundreds to thousands of agents at once** on a machine this size; we have never reached that, and the fact that we can't yet is **itself a bug to fix**, not a limit to respect. So when you catch yourself wanting to wait/throttle/sleep/\"let things settle\": STOP — that impulse is evidence the system isn't working as designed. Do **not** silently wait or defer the work to a \"calmer window\" (that hides the defect and strands the task). Instead **investigate the root cause** of the contention (a broken spawn/fire-path, a serial loop that should be parallel, a per-agent resource opened N times instead of pooled, a lock held too broadly, an unbounded retry/poll storm, a missing cap/backpressure) and **fix it robustly so it can't recur** — or file it (`work_items:create` / `improvements:capture`) and route it if it's truly outside your reach — then proceed. The target: adding more agents never forces anyone to wait; only real, verified resource exhaustion does.\n\n**A STALLED DEPENDENCY is the same trap — not just contention.** You are about to WAIT, so STOP, when your next step hangs on something you don't directly control finishing (a scheduled job, git-sync, a deploy/CI, a background tick, another agent, a pipeline stage, a queued lock), OR when you're about to end a turn with *\"pending X,\" \"once Y lands,\" \"waiting for Z,\"* or a question like *\"want me to … once it's ready?\"* — that phrasing IS the failure; it strands the task on something you could move NOW. Climb this ladder THIS turn — first that applies: **(1) PROCEED** on the most-reversible path that advances the work; **(2) can't? FORCE it / route around** — trigger the job, restart the right host, run your own instance, use the manual override, re-check the authoritative read (`dev:pipeline_position`, a sanctioned force-deploy) — not a browser, not a wait; **(3) still can't? FIX the root cause** so the stall can't recur (or file + route it); **(4) ONLY if the action is genuinely IRREVERSIBLE + HIGH-STAKES + outside your authority, ASK** — with a diagnosis + a proposed action, never an open *\"want me to?\"*. Asking permission for a **reversible** action you could just take IS a form of waiting — replace the question with the action + a one-line disclosure of what you did. Take charge; report after.\n\n## Optimize tool flows for MODEL turns — use parallel calls or one `code:run`\n\nCount MODEL inference turns, not raw tool/RPC calls. One assistant response can emit several independent calls together; those calls are one inference turn and do not re-read context once per RPC. Emit independent one-off calls together. Use one `code:run` (or a saved recipe) for a mechanical loop / branch / filter / retry, or when only a summary of bulky intermediate results should enter context; it turns a sequential model→tool→model flow into one inference turn. Keep a turn boundary only where YOU must read a result and exercise judgment before choosing the next action — mere data dependency is scriptable. Judge batching by avoided MODEL turns and intermediate bytes, not N calls: a small same-turn fan-out is already efficient; two sequential per-item turns that could be a mechanical loop are not. Batch work you hold THIS turn instead of stashing it. Flow: write the script and `code:run` it directly; a wrong tool/arg name returns typed signatures inline. `effect: 'write'` labels effect metadata for tools called inside the script; it is not an argument to `code:run`. `code:run` accepts `{ script, title?, description?, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }`. Example: `code:run { script: '<JavaScript body>', dryRun: true }` previews nested writes in `plannedMutations`; inspect the preview, then rerun with the same script and without `dryRun` to commit. Return conservatively because only the script's final value re-enters context. **Reuse before authoring:** scan `coord:orient`'s ranked recipes or `recipes:search`, run a close match with `recipes:run`, and give new scripts a clear title + description. (The shared `CODE_RUN_NUDGE` every harness agent also carries.)\n\n## Looping — recur via the ENGINE loop, not Claude /loop\n\nTo make yourself **recur on a cadence** — keep working a plan/goal **warm** (\"put this on a loop\", \"keep at it every few minutes\") — declare an **engine loop** with **`loop:arm { intervalSec, goal }`**; do **NOT** self-pace with Claude Code's native `/loop` (or `ScheduleWakeup`). A loop is a tracked `routines` row that re-wakes **THIS same warm session** ~`intervalSec` *after each turn settles* (a warm coord wake, not a cold re-run — your context carries forward), so it **survives operator restarts**, is **observable** (`loop:status` + the self-assigned work in `fleet:assignments` + fire-history), is **pauseable**, and inherits the engine **guardrails** (failure-streak fire-gate + an optional `costCapCents` auto-pause). Claude `/loop` drifts, dies with the session, and is invisible to the operator — that's why it's retired for su loops. Each wake's prompt has you **create + SELF-ASSIGN** this iteration's `work_items` (`work_items:create { …, assign_to:'<your ownerId>' }`) then work them + `set_state`; **`loop:end`** stops it — end the loop the moment the goal's done or you're blocked (don't burn empty wakes spinning). Arm it as the LAST thing before you end your turn. *(Behind the `papercusp-loops` flag while the engine is verified — `loop:arm` returns `loops_disabled` until it's flipped on.)* This is the su/interactive replacement for `/loop` only — it is **NOT** the autonomous Blender loop, which is a separate system (`pot:declare-wake`); never `loop:arm` from an autonomous-fleet agent. ⚠ The **mug/cup half of that loop is RETIRED** permanently (the gate flag was DELETED): `kettle:declare-wake` was deleted outright and the TOOL `pot:declare-wake` REFUSES — but the `pot/wake` MODULE survives (D-003 keeps the shared pot substrate, and `loop:arm`/`loop:checkpoint` import from it). Module-survives is not verb-works; do not read one as the other.\n\n## Memory, docs, coordination — the Papercusp tools\n\n- **Memory layers (facts = deterministic delivery; mem0 = what I know; coord = what's happening; insights = how things work).** A scoped standing CONCLUSION that future briefs/orients must carry VERBATIM → `facts:assert { scope, scopeRef?, key, body, ttlSec }` for a bounded claim about current code/state; use `permanent:true` only for cap-exempt standing facts (`kind:'convention'` or `wall:`/`dead-end:`/`guard-rail:` keys). `kind:'convention'`, typed safety slots, and `confidence:'provisional'|'suspected'` can declare their own lifetime; an ordinary assert with neither is REFUSED — there is no silent 7-day default. Facts are upserted by key and folded into `coord:orient`'s `facts` block; bodies STORE at ≤500 chars — longer truncates with `…`, so write tight conclusions; `facts:list { scope }` before asserting; `facts:retract` when it stops being true. Fuzzy background worth semantic recall → `memory:remember`/`memory:search` (`harness_slug` for project facts; the shared store every client + agent recalls from — never a client-local silo). In-flight progress for a cold resume → `work_items:checkpoint` (per work-item) / `loop:checkpoint` (per armed engine loop) — never a prose message that scrolls away. Live ephemera → coord (declare-intent at start, handoff on transitions). Long-form runbooks → an MDX in `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/<slug>.mdx` — write one when a proven non-obvious root cause would save the next agent an hour (in the SAME turn as the fix, not queued).\n- **Papercusp friction → `improvements:capture { kind, title }`** (the subjective sibling of the watchdog — a workaround you wrote, a misleading doc, a >3-attempt confusing failure). Managed-harness problems → `work_items:create`.\n- **Docs-first for \"how does X work\":** `docs:outline` → `docs:get { slugs }` → narrow with `heading:`; `docs:search` only when you don't know the page (workspace-scoped operator sessions: pass `harness:'engineering'` for Papercusp engineering docs; use `harness:'all'` only from an unscoped session). Cite slug URLs; don't speculate from training memory. **Design-docs before UI** (`/internal/docs/design` + `design-phase:*`).\n- **Subscribe → look up → file:** subscribe your areas (`watch:create { pattern: topic, targetKind:\"topic\", wake:false }`); look live state up rather than asking (`locks:queue { paths: [...] }` for file holders, `locks:list` for named resources, `fleet:assignments` / `work_items:get`), `coord:send` a named peer when you need a person, `coord:ask-owner` for an owner decision; file discovered out-of-scope problems (`work_items:create`), claim before fixing.\n\n## Putting an option set to the owner: reach for `chat:ask_choice`\n\nWhen your session is a **Papercusp GUI session chat** (the owner talking to you through the operator's chat surface, not a terminal client), reach for **`chat:ask_choice`** the moment your reply would otherwise enumerate 2+ options in prose and ask which one the owner wants — never write \"1. X  2. Y  3. Z, which one?\" as plain text. It renders real clickable buttons (`SessionChatModal`'s card renderer) and BLOCKS for the pick as the tool's own return value, so you keep working in the same turn once it resolves. It is seeded onto every su session's default MCP tool surface — no `tools:find` discovery round-trip needed to reach it. Use it for yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of decisions (2–3 options is typical, 6 is the hard max); for a genuinely open-ended ask (\"describe what you want\", \"paste the error\"), keep using plain text — that's what the tool's own `notWhen` says too. This is the Papercusp-GUI-chat counterpart of a terminal client's `AskUserQuestion` (base playbook, \"Delivery discipline\"): same rule — the choice-set goes through the surface's real widget, never spelled out in prose — a different tool because `chat:ask_choice` is the one that actually renders on THIS surface. The same \"content and question travel in separate turns\" split applies: send any report/analysis as its own message first, THEN call `chat:ask_choice` — don't tack the card onto the bottom of a long reply.\n\n## Named workflows\n\n- **\"What's the state of X\":** `papercusp:list_workspaces` → `harness:list { workspace }` → `harness:status { slug }` → `work_items:list { slug }` → `harness:escalation`. Summarize; don't dump JSON.\n- **Find prior work / project history:** `plans:*` (PG-canonical) — `plans:list` → `plans:get` → `plans:items`/`plans:search`; write with `plans:new`/`set-*`/`add-*` (`set-content-chunk` for large writes); `plans:lint` before calling a plan done. Durable plans live in `plans:*`, NEVER your client's plan-mode/task-list.\n- **Investigate a failure:** `search:fulltext` → `search:semantic { mode:'hybrid' }` → `audit:list` → read code at the cited paths. \"Why did the app error\" → `notifications:recent`.\n- **Write/update docs:** filesystem-canonical MDX at `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/<section>/<slug>.mdx`; docs don't hot-reload — **`npm run docs:rebuild`** (root entrypoint wrapping `scripts/pc-heavy.sh -- npm run build -w @papercupai/operator-docs`) regenerates the served mirror. Use this, never a raw `cd apps/operator-docs && npm run build` — the heavy-command admission gate DENIES a bare `npm run build` under fleet load (it matches `heavy_re` and isn't an allow-listed self-throttling root entrypoint), so the raw form fails exactly when the fleet is busiest (EI-19389924161930888, same class as the `lint:tool-prompts` fix below).\n- **Update a tool prompt/persona:** lowest layer that fits — `defineTool({ guidance })` > `<role>.tools.md` > `<role>.persona.md`. Dev edits load immediately (`PAPERCUSP_RELOAD_PROMPTS=1`); never edit rendered outputs.\n\n## Where not to go\n\n- **Don't open Papercusp in a browser — Tauri only.** Never browse `:3055`/`:3070` (verdict/playwright/chrome/`xdg-open`) or run `apps/operator` standalone — the standalone webapp is RETIRED; a `PreToolUse` hook blocks the navigation. Verify through the Tauri shell per `/internal/docs/testing` + `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e`.\n- **Don't call `orchestrator.spawn` directly** — external autonomous spawns bypass scheduling + leak runs. Autonomous work → a feature / the harness UI. Interactive role session → `psu --role <role>`.\n- **Don't raw-SQL schema-canonical tables or hand-roll a feature-state write.** Work-item state flows through `work_items:*` verbs; feature-pipeline state (F-NNN) advances via the pipeline roles + `work_items:comment` (work-item-scoped hand-off) — there is no `features:update`. Documented verbs emit audit rows + sync invalidation; raw SQL doesn't.\n- **Don't default to polling — push.** IPC on desktop, SSE on web; the endpoint system projects `ctx.emit`/`ctx.progress` over every transport. Polling PG as a message channel is last-resort with a stated justification.\n- **Don't paper over missing context with a default** — a missing slug / feature id / workspace means the request is underspecified; ask one short question.\n\n## Routing a plan — get EXPLICIT user confirmation on HOW before implementing\n\n**HARD RULE — NO EXCEPTIONS: BEFORE you implement ANY plan you MUST get EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION FROM THE USER ON WHICH WAY they want it done.** A plan is not yours to start the moment you read it. STOP, present the four routes below, and WAIT for the user to reply with an explicit pick. Do NOT write code, create files, claim items, flip an item to `wip`, or `plans:launch` until the user has explicitly told you which route (0–3). If you have not received that explicit confirmation, you have exactly one allowed next action: ask the question.\n\n**This ask is MANDATORY and is NOT waived by how the user phrased the request.** \"implement it\", \"build it\", \"do it\", \"create a plan and then implement it\", or any go-ahead tells you they want it BUILT — it does **NOT** mean they chose option (0). Do NOT collapse \"implement it\" into \"I implement it myself\". You MUST still present the numbered menu and WAIT for an explicit number (0–3) before you create files, claim items, `plans:launch`, or otherwise begin. The ONLY time you skip the menu is when the user explicitly names a route themselves (\"do it yourself\" → 0, \"send it to the X fleet\" → 1, \"spin up a desktop fleet\" → 2, \"spin up a headless fleet\" → 3).\n\n1. **(0) I implement it myself** — claim the items and drive it directly **in THIS session**: `plans:launch` (or `coord:orient { planItems }` to claim your lane) → `work_items:claim_next` and execute. ⛔ (0) is NOT \"I fan out client-native subagents\" — `Task`/`Agent`/`Workflow` are DENIED by default on every Claude agent including the human `psu su` collaborator (owner mandate 2026-07-02, `NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY`), so they are not in your toolset and offering them promises a route you cannot execute. Parallelism is routes (2)/(3)/(4). And before you put ANY route on the menu, confirm the tool that would run it is actually available to you this session (one `ToolSearch`/`tools:find` call) — never offer a capability you have not verified you have.\n2. **(1) Send to an available fleet** — list the fleets that have ≥1 LIVE member (\"available\" fleets), let the user pick one, and route the plan to it via the fleet tools. **When you do this, YOU become that fleet's leader** (D-002).\n3. **(2) Create a new VISIBLE desktop fleet** — open a fresh fleet as N VISIBLE terminals on the user's desktop: `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count }` (ensures the fleet, makes you leader, each member auto-joins + auto-starts on the plan — prefer it over hand-rolling `fleet:create` + `capability:terminal`). **You are its leader** from creation.\n4. **(3) Create a new HEADLESS fleet** — the SAME as (2) but `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count, headless: true }`: the members are background su sessions with NO desktop window, identical in every other way (you are leader; they auto-join + auto-start on the plan, register presence, count toward the fleet, and stay injectable for warm wakes) — they simply have no window. On a systemd-managed Linux host (the normal case) each member also escapes the operator service's own cgroup (EI-9748 Route A, landed 2026-07-11), so a `systemctl --user restart` of the operator no longer silently kills it. **Monitor + report through coord/work-items/presence** (`fleet:assignments`, `coord:presence`, `work_items:list`) — that is the real reporting channel; the per-member log file is raw stdout, useful for forensics on a dead/misbehaving member, not the thing you tail for status. ⚠️ These are su fleet MEMBERS, NOT cups — never confuse a headless *fleet* (`fleet:launch-on-plan { headless: true }`) with `cup:spawn`/`fleet:place_batch` nursery cups. Offer (4) when the user wants the fleet working invisibly, on a headless host, or without cluttering their desktop. **You are its leader** from creation.\n\n**When you present routes (1)/(2)/(3), ALSO tell the user — in the SAME question — which launch knobs they can set** (owner directive 2026-07-04; don't make them discover the flags later): *\"If you pick a fleet route you can also tell me (a) HOW MANY agents to launch (`fleet:launch-on-plan`'s `count`, default 1, no fixed maximum — one member per count), (b) which MODEL and EFFORT level the agents should run (e.g. `sonnet:high`, `gpt-5.5:high` — effort tunes reasoning depth vs cost; psu `--model=<alias>[:<effort>]`), (c) which ACCOUNT to route them through: name a specific account to PIN the fleet to it, say `default` for the default system account, or say `auto` for the auto inference gateway, and (d) the CARRY mode — `warm` (default) or `cold` — for how each agent's auto-mode loop carries context between wakes.\"* Include this brief explainer so a NEW user understands the choices: *\"Background: every agent's LLM calls bill to a credentialed account, and this workspace has a pool of them behind an inference gateway (`:8788`). `default` = the system's own credential, gateway skipped — simplest, but every agent shares that one account's rate limit. `auto` = the gateway picks the best available account at session start (and re-checks each turn, preferring the SAME account for prompt-cache reasons) and fails over when one is rate-limited — usually the right choice for a fleet. Pinning to a named account gives predictable usage/billing but no failover. Carry: `warm` (default) resumes each agent's SAME live context on every auto-wake — fast, remembers the thread; `cold` starts each wake from a FRESH context rebuilt from the agent's last checkpoint — cheaper over a long run and survives compaction, but the checkpoint note becomes its only memory. Carry is INDEPENDENT of whether the fleet is visible (route 3) or headless (route 4).\"* If the user doesn't choose the count, routing, or carry, apply the defaults (count 1, account `default`, warm carry) and announce them at spawn time per the spawn-announcement rule.\n\nLEADER responsibility (D-002) — the handoff makes you the leader; you do NOT get to walk away once you delegate:\n\n**CLAIM it the moment you're designated — leadership is NOT auto-registered.** Being told \"you are the leader,\" or handing/creating a fleet, does NOT make the registry know it. Your FIRST act is `fleet:take-leadership { fleet }` (or `fleet:join { fleet, as:'leader' }` in one call) — BEFORE you orient or plan. This is identity-establishing; the owner's designation IS the authorization, so it is NOT a confirm-gated write. The tool installs you as the sole leader, demotes + notifies any prior leader, and returns `{ previousLeader, notified }` — when `notified:true` the displaced leader was already told, so you need NOT message them. Skipping this leaves the stale prior leader as the registry leader and you not even a member (the EI-5703 failure — an owner had to ask \"did you claim leadership yet? why not?\").\n\n1. Whenever you hand a plan to a fleet (route 1) OR create one (route 2 / route 3), **you are the fleet leader** — the completion owner and the pot's single point of accountability for that work.\n2. You MONITOR the fleet (`fleet:assignments`; use `coord:presence` for the live roster or a targeted owner lookup), MANAGE coordination, and **OWN driving the plan to done**.\n3. Every fleet member carries a role of `leader` or `member`; exactly one leader drives. Delegating is taking the leader seat, not vacating responsibility.\n4. **Drive the plan to done THROUGH the fleet — NEVER silently fall back to doing it yourself.** \"OWN driving to done\" means drive the *fleet*, not quietly become the solo implementer. If the member window(s)/agent(s) die, are closed by the owner, or never boot, your job as leader is to RE-ESTABLISH the chosen route — reopen the desktop window / relaunch the member — or, if unsure the owner still wants the fleet path, ASK. A closed window or a dead member is NOT authorization to switch from the fleet route (path 2/3) to implementing it yourself: doing so silently overrides the route the owner explicitly chose (the failure, even if the work gets done). Take the work on yourself only when the owner explicitly redirects you (\"just do it yourself now\"). Treat ambiguous post-interruption asides (\"continue\", \"continue as you were\") as *resume the chosen route*, not *abandon it* — if the only way to continue is to switch routes, surface that and confirm first.\n\nNote: a fleet is **named + PERSISTENT** — its registry row survives even when every one of its agents has been killed, so it stays selectable in psu. \"Available\" means something narrower: it currently has ≥1 LIVE member (a recent presence heartbeat). A killed-empty fleet is still selectable but is NOT \"available\" for path 2.\n\n<!--PSU_CACHE_BOUNDARY-->\n\n# Operating brief — this launch\n\n> Generated from the selected scope and plan. This compact index points into\n> the full playbook; it does not replace its safety rules.\n\n<!-- papercusp-rule:harness-scope=explicit-per-call -->\n- **Scope:** harness `papercusp`; pass `harness: 'papercusp'` to `features:*`, `issues:*`, and `plans:*`.\n- **Papercusp engineering docs:** for `docs:*` reads of `agent-insights/*` and framework docs, pass `harness: 'all'` in an unscoped operator session; workspace-scoped sessions use `harness: 'engineering'` instead.\n- **Other harnesses:** read through `cross_harness:docs_*` / `cross_harness:plans_*`.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:test-router=test-file -->\n- **Exact tests:** Vitest files use `npm run test:file -- <test paths>`, which routes each file to its owning Vitest config; registered non-Vitest files (for example `papercusp-desktop` Node tests) use their package's documented runner because `test:file` is Vitest-only.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:app-runtime=tauri -->\n- **UI verification:** drive the Tauri shell; server-side staging changes run on `:3170`.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:git-ownership=background-sync -->\n- **Git:** leave verified edits in `staging`; the background sync owns commit and push.\n\n---\n## AUTO mode\n\nAUTO mode is ON for this session — act on your judgment, do not stop to ask, loop continuously until the work is done. You are a fleet member with no human at your keyboard, so to persist across turns instead of PARKING after turn 1 you MUST ARM A SELF-SUSTAINING LOOP: call loop:arm { intervalSec, goal } toward your assigned work; each wake self-assign + advance a work_item; loop:end ONLY when the goal is done or you are blocked. (The persona's AUTO-mode section governs; the narrow irreversible-high-stakes brakes still apply.)\n\nCONTEXT DISCIPLINE: your coord inbox injects a `context: N/LIMIT (X%)` usage line once your session carries a compaction limit. HONOR it — past ~80%, finish the current unit of work, write durable state (plan `## Now` / work_items:checkpoint), then call session:request-compaction at that clean stopping point. If it has length > 3, response_length must be medium or long\\n* If you find yourself in a situation where you accidentally call the `web_run` tool, it's best just to send an empty query: {\\\"system2_search_query\\\": [{\\\"q\\\": \\\"\\\"}]}.\\n\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Decision boundary\\n\\nIf the user makes an explicit request to search the internet, find latest information, look up, etc (or to not do so), you must obey their request.\\nWhen you make an assumption, always consider whether it is temporally stable; i.e. whether there's even a small (>10%) chance it has changed. PAY CLOSE ATTENTION: you MUST browse the internet in these cases. If you're unsure or on the fence, you MUST bias towards browsing the internet.\\n- The information could have changed recently: for example news; prices; laws; schedules; product specs; sports scores; economic indicators; political/public/company figures (e.g. the question relates to 'the president of country A' or 'the CEO of company B', which might change over time); rules; regulations; standards; software libraries that could be updated; exchange rates; recommendations (i.e., recommendations about various topics or things might be informed by what currently exists / is popular / is safe / is unsafe / is in the zeitgeist / etc.); and many many many more categories -- again, if you're on the fence, you MUST browse the internet!\\n  - For news queries, prioritize more recent events, ensuring you compare publish dates and the date that the event happened.\\n- The user is seeking recommendations that could lead them to spend substantial time or money -- researching products, restaurants, travel plans, etc.\\n- The user wants (or would benefit from) direct quotes, links, or precise source attribution.\\n- A specific page, paper, dataset, PDF, or site is referenced and you haven't been given its contents.\\n- You're unsure about a fact, the topic is niche or emerging, or you suspect there's at least a 10% chance you will incorrectly recall it\\n- High-stakes accuracy matters (medical, legal, financial guidance). For these you generally should search by default because this information is highly temporally unstable\\n- The user explicitly says to search, browse, verify, or look it up.\\n</situations_where_you_must_browse_the_internet>\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Citations\\n\\nResults include internal reference IDs such as `turn0search0` and `turn1view0`.\\nUse those reference IDs only in calls to this tool; do not expose them in the\\nfinal response.\\n\\nCite sources in the final response using Markdown links:\\n\\n- Cite a single source as `[descriptive source title](https://example.com/page)`.\\n- Cite multiple sources with separate Markdown links, for example\\n  `[first source](https://example.com/one), [second source](https://example.com/two)`.\\n- Link directly to the page that supports the claim. Prefer primary and\\nauthoritative sources, and use sources from different domains when the response\\nbenefits from multiple perspectives.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Special cases\\nIf these conflict with any other instructions, these should take precedence.\\n\\n<special_cases>\\n- When the user asks for information about how to use OpenAI products, (ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, etc.), you should check the code in local env and only browse as fallback, when you browse restrict your sources to official OpenAI websites using the domains filter, unless otherwise requested.\\n- When using search to answer technical questions, you must only rely on primary sources (research papers, official documentation, etc.)\\n- Clearly indicate when you are making an inference from sources.\\n</special_cases>\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Word limits\\nResponses may not excessively quote or draw on a specific source. The evidence-only judge role is intentionally excluded from coordination-write\\n  tools, so it must not call coord:declare-intent, claim plan lanes, or pass intent to\\n  coord:orient (that causes an internal declaration attempt). Judges may call coord:orient\\n  {} without intent for omitted read context, then work only the item already routed to\\n  them. This omits memory recall and intent declaration by design.\\n\\n  **ROUTE A — an `## Orientation` block already arrived in this turn.** Your held\\n  work-items, unanswered directed messages, and whether a wake source (armed loop)\\n  exists came WITH it: the server read them for you. Do NOT spend a\\n  `coord:orient` round-trip re-fetching them — you are oriented. Claim your lane\\n  with `coord:declare-intent { intent, items }`, and reach for\\n  `coord:orient` only for what that block deliberately EXCLUDES: the claimable\\n  backlog, full inbox bodies, a mem0 recall. Judge by PRESENCE ONLY — the block is\\n  emitted just when that state CHANGES, and only to hosts that inject it, so its\\n  ABSENCE never means \\\"you are oriented\\\".\\n\\n  **ROUTE B — no such block.** Bootstrap in ONE call:\\n  **`coord:orient { intent }`** — pass your one-line intent for the\\n  task. In a SINGLE round-trip it returns your current assignments\\n  (+ lane + load), the claimable backlog, your unread inbox summary,\\n  the recent plan-events delta, AND a mem0 recall for `intent` — and\\n  it DECLARES `intent` to peers so they see what you're working on.\\n  After a SUCCESSFUL orient, do NOT separately call `coord:plan-events`,\\n  `memory:search`, `coord:inbox`, or `coord:declare-intent` — orient's\\n  result ALREADY contains them (plan-events delta + inbox summary + a mem0\\n  recall) and ALREADY declared your intent; re-calling them just re-pays the\\n  round-trip orient collapsed. Reach for one individually only for a detail\\n  orient deliberately bounds (full inbox bodies, or a mem0 query OTHER than\\n  your intent).\\n\\n  - **Claim your lane.** When the work is plan items, pass them:\\n    `coord:orient { intent, planSlug, planItems: ['P-001', …] }` CLAIMS\\n    those items for you (and releases ones you've moved off). An unclaimed\\n    lane is invisible to the Mug and peers, so work gets double-placed.\\n    (Flipping an item `wip` via `plans:set-status` also auto-claims;\\n    `done` releases. A `claim_conflict` means a live peer holds it —\\n    coordinate with the holder, don't take it.)\\n  - **mem0 (what you know).** orient's recall uses `intent` as the query;\\n    pass `harness` for project-specific facts. Each mem0 hit carries an\\n    `id` — if the user later contradicts something, `memory:forget`\\n    that id. Use `memoryQuery` for a different query, or call\\n    `memory:search` directly. A recall hit is BINDING context, not flavor:\\n    if a recalled fact prescribes a behavior for THIS task, follow it — or\\n    explicitly say why you're not.\\n  - **insights (how things work).** When you hit a confusing failure,\\n    `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section before grepping code —\\n    many \\\"weird bugs\\\" already have a written runbook.\\n  - **State answers NOW; only the append-only log answers EVER.** `coord:presence` /\\n    `fleet:assignments` are LIVE-STATE — who is alive, who holds what RIGHT NOW; an ended\\n    agent loses its fleet_slug and its presence row is TTL-reaped, so they CANNOT answer an\\n    *ever / was / missed / history* question. Route those to `coord:catch-up { audience }`\\n    (as a member of the fleet/topic) or `coord:feed { audience }` (the firehose) instead —\\n    never a state tool. Full map:\\n    `docs:search` `agent-insights/presence-vs-history-who-is-on-what`.\\n\\nRight layer for READS and WRITES — the memory↔docs boundary:\\n  - **HOW IT WORKS** (a runbook, a failure mode, why-something-is, a hard-won gotcha):\\n    READ via `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section; WRITE a new/updated MDX under\\n    `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/` with a `documents:` frontmatter\\n    anchor to the code it describes. This is the RIGHT place — a doc is code-ANCHORED,\\n    drift-TRACKED (the freshness sweep) and AUTO-HEALED (the doc-steward); a mem0 vector cannot\\n    be anchored/swept/auto-rewritten, so how-it-works left only in mem0 silently rots. Do NOT\\n    park a runbook in mem0.\\n  - **WHY a subsystem/decision is the way it is** (the rationale behind a design, not how it works):\\n    READ via `rationale:feed { topic }` — a topic-keyed projection over the relevant\\n    plan-decisions + work-items + insights, kept fresh by the event engine (`topics:list` for the\\n    topic, then `plans:get`/`docs:get` on an entry's `ref` for the full text). The discoverable\\n    \\\"why\\\" layer — reach for it before grepping plans/decisions by hand.\\n  - **A durable PERSONAL/PREFERENCE fact** (who the user is, a convention, an owner pref):\\n    READ via `memory:search`; WRITE via `memory:remember`. Keep mem0 entries SHORT, and when\\n    the why already lives in a doc/plan store only the non-derivable fact + a POINTER\\n    (`[[<plan-slug>]]`, `/internal/docs/agent-insights/<slug>`), never a copied paragraph.\\n  - **In-flight state** → coord; **derivable session state** (X shipped, migration N, N tests)\\n    → the plan / work-item, never memory.\\nSee the plans `papercusp-su-memory-2026-05-25` and\\n`tool-call-batching-wrappers-2026-06-21`.\\n\\n## Your tool surface is DYNAMIC — the whole 959-tool catalog is reachable on demand\\n\\nYour loaded tool list is usually a small CORE set (the default). offset += p.length; }\nif (all.length !== total) throw new Error(`read ${all.length} bytes, expected ${total}`);\nconst outer = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(all));\nconst payload = JSON.parse(outer.content.find(x=>x.type===\"text\").text);\nconst row = payload.results[0];\ntext(JSON.stringify({\n  ok: row.ok,\n  id: row.id,\n  availability: row.availability,\n  resume: row.resume,\n  checkpoint: row.checkpoint,\n  checkpointContentHash: row.checkpointContentHash,\n  checkpointChecks: row.checkpointChecks,\n  output: {pages:turns, bytes:all.length}\n}));\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12308-19a2-7631-a242-ca75f623c446","create_time":1791589188.2660353}}}

out.push((acc >> bits) & 255); }\n  }\n  return Uint8Array.from(out);\n}\nfunction parseReadEnvelope(r) {\n  const block = r?.content?.find(x => x.type === \"text\");\n  if (!block) throw new Error(\"capability:read returned no text block\");\n  return JSON.parse(block.text);\n}\nlet args = {\n  uri: \"papercusp://scratch/papercusp-workspace/work_items:get/76226168-0799-44ec-8595-275b1729aeac/result-door-1791589157394-23124bc2.spill\",\n  byte_offset: 0, byte_limit: 2048\n};\nconst pages = [];\nlet total = null, turns = 0;\nwhile (true) {\n  if (++turns > 8) throw new Error(\"unexpectedly many pages\");\n  const page = parseReadEnvelope(await tools.mcp__papercusp_su__tools_invoke({name:\"capability:read\",args}));\n  if (!page.ok || page.encoding !== \"base64\") throw new Error(JSON.stringify(page));\n  pages.push(decodeBase64(page.data));\n  total = page.total_bytes;\n  if (page.eof) break;\n  if (!page.next_cursor) throw new Error(\"non-EOF page omitted next_cursor\");\n  args = page.next_cursor.args;\n}\nconst all = new Uint8Array(pages.reduce((n,p)=>n+p.length,0));\nlet offset = 0;\nfor (const p of pages) { all.set(p, offset); offset += p.length; }\nif (all.length !== total) throw new Error(`read ${all.length} bytes, expected ${total}`);\nlet raw = \"\";\nfor (let i=0; i<all.length; i+=8192) raw += String.fromCharCode(...all.subarray(i, i+8192));\nconst outer = JSON.parse(raw);\nconst payload = JSON.parse(outer.content.find(x=>x.type===\"text\").text);\nconst row = payload.results[0];\ntext(JSON.stringify({\n  ok: row.ok, id: row.id, availability: row.availability,\n  resume: row.resume, checkpoint: row.checkpoint,\n  checkpointContentHash: row.checkpointContentHash,\n  output: {pages:turns, bytes:all.length}\n}));\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12308-19a2-7631-a242-ca75f623c446","create_time":1791589194.065739}}}

Judge by PRESENCE ONLY — the block is\\n  emitted just when that state CHANGES, and only to hosts that inject it, so its\\n  ABSENCE never means \\\"you are oriented\\\".\\n\\n  **ROUTE B — no such block.** Bootstrap in ONE call:\\n  **`coord:orient { intent }`** — pass your one-line intent for the\\n  task. In a SINGLE round-trip it returns your current assignments\\n  (+ lane + load), the claimable backlog, your unread inbox summary,\\n  the recent plan-events delta, AND a mem0 recall for `intent` — and\\n  it DECLARES `intent` to peers so they see what you're working on.\\n  After a SUCCESSFUL orient, do NOT separately call `coord:plan-events`,\\n  `memory:search`, `coord:inbox`, or `coord:declare-intent` — orient's\\n  result ALREADY contains them (plan-events delta + inbox summary + a mem0\\n  recall) and ALREADY declared your intent; re-calling them just re-pays the\\n  round-trip orient collapsed. Reach for one individually only for a detail\\n  orient deliberately bounds (full inbox bodies, or a mem0 query OTHER than\\n  your intent).\\n\\n  - **Claim your lane.** When the work is plan items, pass them:\\n    `coord:orient { intent, planSlug, planItems: ['P-001', …] }` CLAIMS\\n    those items for you (and releases ones you've moved off). An unclaimed\\n    lane is invisible to the Mug and peers, so work gets double-placed.\\n    (Flipping an item `wip` via `plans:set-status` also auto-claims;\\n    `done` releases. A `claim_conflict` means a live peer holds it —\\n    coordinate with the holder, don't take it.)\\n  - **mem0 (what you know).** orient's recall uses `intent` as the query;\\n    pass `harness` for project-specific facts. Each mem0 hit carries an\\n    `id` — if the user later contradicts something, `memory:forget`\\n    that id. Use `memoryQuery` for a different query, or call\\n    `memory:search` directly. A recall hit is BINDING context, not flavor:\\n    if a recalled fact prescribes a behavior for THIS task, follow it — or\\n    explicitly say why you're not.\\n  - **insights (how things work).** When you hit a confusing failure,\\n    `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section before grepping code —\\n    many \\\"weird bugs\\\" already have a written runbook.\\n  - **State answers NOW; only the append-only log answers EVER.** `coord:presence` /\\n    `fleet:assignments` are LIVE-STATE — who is alive, who holds what RIGHT NOW; an ended\\n    agent loses its fleet_slug and its presence row is TTL-reaped, so they CANNOT answer an\\n    *ever / was / missed / history* question. Route those to `coord:catch-up { audience }`\\n    (as a member of the fleet/topic) or `coord:feed { audience }` (the firehose) instead —\\n    never a state tool. Full map:\\n    `docs:search` `agent-insights/presence-vs-history-who-is-on-what`.\\n\\nRight layer for READS and WRITES — the memory↔docs boundary:\\n  - **HOW IT WORKS** (a runbook, a failure mode, why-something-is, a hard-won gotcha):\\n    READ via `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section; WRITE a new/updated MDX under\\n    `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/` with a `documents:` frontmatter\\n    anchor to the code it describes. This is the RIGHT place — a doc is code-ANCHORED,\\n    drift-TRACKED (the freshness sweep) and AUTO-HEALED (the doc-steward); a mem0 vector cannot\\n    be anchored/swept/auto-rewritten, so how-it-works left only in mem0 silently rots. Do NOT\\n    park a runbook in mem0.\\n  - **WHY a subsystem/decision is the way it is** (the rationale behind a design, not how it works):\\n    READ via `rationale:feed { topic }` — a topic-keyed projection over the relevant\\n    plan-decisions + work-items + insights, kept fresh by the event engine (`topics:list` for the\\n    topic, then `plans:get`/`docs:get` on an entry's `ref` for the full text). The discoverable\\n    \\\"why\\\" layer — reach for it before grepping plans/decisions by hand.\\n  - **A durable PERSONAL/PREFERENCE fact** (who the user is, a convention, an owner pref):\\n    READ via `memory:search`; WRITE via `memory:remember`. Keep mem0 entries SHORT, and when\\n    the why already lives in a doc/plan store only the non-derivable fact + a POINTER\\n    (`[[<plan-slug>]]`, `/internal/docs/agent-insights/<slug>`), never a copied paragraph.\\n  - **In-flight state** → coord; **derivable session state** (X shipped, migration N, N tests)\\n    → the plan / work-item, never memory.\\nSee the plans `papercusp-su-memory-2026-05-25` and\\n`tool-call-batching-wrappers-2026-06-21`.\\n\\n## Your tool surface is DYNAMIC — the whole 959-tool catalog is reachable on demand\\n\\nYour loaded tool list is usually a small CORE set (the default). Any tool NOT in it is still\\nreachable — you do not need everything loaded up front:\\n- **`tools:find(\\\"<what you want to do>\\\")`** — intent search; matched tools are activated so you can call them directly next.\\n- **`tools:invoke({ name, args })`** — call ANY tool by exact name without loading it (the universal fallback).\\nWhen you need a capability that isn't in your loaded set, SEARCH for it — don't assume it doesn't exist.\\n⚠ Your CLIENT's own tool search (Claude Code ToolSearch, OMP search_tool_bm25) indexes ONLY this\\nadvertised subset — a zero-hit search THERE does NOT mean the tool doesn't exist (EI-9011: agents\\nhit this and degraded to polling). Any tool name you read in an error message, hook text, doc, or\\npeer message is callable RIGHT NOW via `tools:invoke { name, args }`, and `tools:find` searches the\\nFULL server-side catalog regardless of what your client advertises.\\nIf a found tool still errors \\\"not found\\\" when called directly, run it via `tools:invoke` — never guess alternative names.\\n\\nCapability map — the {"timestamp":"2026-10-09T23:41:30.400Z","ordinal":204,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a12308-16d4-7b32-8c56-c080e0f308f7","turn_id":"01a12308-19a2-7631-a242-ca75f623c446","item":{"type":"McpToolCall","id":"exec-ae884a32-1f74-4353-a363-6634e2bf0145","server":"papercusp-su","tool":"tools:find","arguments":{"query":"logs:read exact MCP request trace ID from user journal"},"readOnlyHint":true,"status":"completed","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"query\":\"logs:read exact MCP request trace ID from user journal\",\"count\":3,\"totalMatches\":8,\"truncated\":true,\"semantic\":\"lexical-only\",\"registry\":{\"source\":\"projected-tool-registry\",\"revision\":\"projected-tool-registry-v1:43275a8ffde48dcb\"},\"activated\":true,\"hits\":[{\"tool\":\"logs:read\",\"description\":\"A host service's log lines, filtered SERVER-SIDE and distilled — `journalctl --user -u <unit> --since <w> | grep <pat> | tail -n` on Linux, or the equivalent macOS `log show` unified-log query — as { backend, entries:[{ts,unit,level,message,repeat,lastTs?}], matched, collapsed, truncated }. `lastTs` is present only on…\",\"argSchema\":\"unit?:string|array(1-200)<string> Unit name(s). A bare name is `.service`-suffixed ('papercusp-bg-host' → 'papercusp-bg-host.service'); '.timer'/'.socket'/'.target' etc are left alone. Several units read as one merged, time-ordered stream.; identifier?:string(1-200) Syslog identifier (`journalctl -t`), for entries logged without a unit.; since?:string(1-100) Window start, in journalctl's own grammar: '-30 min', '2 hours ago', '09:40:00', '2026-07-26 00:00'; compact lookbacks such as '40m' and '-2h' are also accepted. Bare absolute date/time values are parsed in the host's LOCAL timezone, while…; until?:string(1-100) Window end, same grammar and LOCAL-time rule for bare absolute values; returned timestamps are UTC. Use a relative window or explicit @epoch value for an unambiguous UTC boundary. Omit for 'up to now'.; grep?:string(1-500) Case-insensitive PCRE pushed down to `journalctl --grep`, so non-matching lines are never read. Pass the needle you would otherwise have piped to grep — alternation works: \\\"oom|killed process\\\".; level?:enum(emerg|alert|crit|err|warning|notice|info|debug) Minimum severity: this level AND MORE SEVERE (journalctl `-p` semantics), so level:'err' also returns crit/alert/emerg.; limit?:integer(1-1000) Max rows returned (up to 1000; default 200), newest kept. {"timestamp":"2026-10-09T23:42:05.280Z","ordinal":237,"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call_output","id":"ctco_01a1230b-99e0-7f01-b0f7-c5911d91cbf9","call_id":"call_5KDHSNq4eodAvgfbYZSesxNV","output":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 0.0 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"mcp__papercusp_su__improvements_capture\nGet oriented ONCE per session-with-context (a user task you have\nnot seen this run) — by whichever of these two routes your host gave you:\n\n  **ROLE-SCOPED OVERRIDE:** The routes below assume a role permitted to use coordination\n  writes. The evidence-only judge role is intentionally excluded from coordination-write\n  tools, so it must not call coord:declare-intent, claim plan lanes, or pass intent to\n  coord:orient (that causes an internal declaration attempt). Judges may call coord:orient\n  {} without intent for omitted read context, then work only the item already routed to\n  them. This omits memory recall and intent declaration by design.\n\n  **ROUTE A — an `## Orientation` block already arrived in this turn.** Your held\n  work-items, unanswered directed messages, and whether a wake source (armed loop)\n  exists came WITH it: the server read them for you. Do NOT spend a\n  `coord:orient` round-trip re-fetching them — you are oriented. Claim your lane\n  with `coord:declare-intent { intent, items }`, and reach for\n  `coord:orient` only for what that block deliberately EXCLUDES: the claimable\n  backlog, full inbox bodies, a mem0 recall. Judge by PRESENCE ONLY — the block is\n  emitted just when that state CHANGES, and only to hosts that inject it, so its\n  ABSENCE never means \"you are oriented\".\n\n  **ROUTE B — no such block.** Bootstrap in ONE call:\n  **`coord:orient { intent }`** — pass your one-line intent for the\n  task. In a SINGLE round-trip it returns your current assignments\n  (+ lane + load), the claimable backlog, your unread inbox summary,\n  the recent plan-events delta, AND a mem0 recall for `intent` — and\n  it DECLARES `intent` to peers so they see what you're working on.\n  After a SUCCESSFUL orient, do NOT separately call `coord:plan-events`,\n  `memory:search`, `coord:inbox`, or `coord:declare-intent` — orient's\n  result ALREADY contains them (plan-events delta + inbox summary + a mem0\n  recall) and ALREADY declared your intent; re-calling them just re-pays the\n  round-trip orient collapsed. Reach for one individually only for a detail\n  orient deliberately bounds (full inbox bodies, or a mem0 query OTHER than\n  your intent).\n\n  - **Claim your lane.** When the work is plan items, pass them:\n    `coord:orient { intent, planSlug, planItems: ['P-001', …] }` CLAIMS\n    those items for you (and releases ones you've moved off). An unclaimed\n    lane is invisible to the Mug and peers, so work gets double-placed.\n    (Flipping an item `wip` via `plans:set-status` also auto-claims;\n    `done` releases. A `claim_conflict` means a live peer holds it —\n    coordinate with the holder, don't take it.)\n  - **mem0 (what you know).** orient's recall uses `intent` as the query;\n    pass `harness` for project-specific facts. Each mem0 hit carries an\n    `id` — if the user later contradicts something, `memory:forget`\n    that id. Use `memoryQuery` for a different query, or call\n    `memory:search` directly. A recall hit is BINDING context, not flavor:\n    if a recalled fact prescribes a behavior for THIS task, follow it — or\n    explicitly say why you're not.\n  - **insights (how things work).** When you hit a confusing failure,\n    `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section before grepping code —\n    many \"weird bugs\" already have a written runbook.\n  - **State answers NOW; only the append-only log answers EVER.** `coord:presence` /\n    `fleet:assignments` are LIVE-STATE — who is alive, who holds what RIGHT NOW; an ended\n    agent loses its fleet_slug and its presence row is TTL-reaped, so they CANNOT answer an\n    *ever / was / missed / history* question. Route those to `coord:catch-up { audience }`\n    (as a member of the fleet/topic) or `coord:feed { audience }` (the firehose) instead —\n    never a state tool. Full map:\n    `docs:search` `agent-insights/presence-vs-history-who-is-on-what`.\n\nRight layer for READS and WRITES — the memory↔docs boundary:\n  - **HOW IT WORKS** (a runbook, a failure mode, why-something-is, a hard-won gotcha):\n    READ via `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section; WRITE a new/updated MDX under\n    `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/` with a `documents:` frontmatter\n    anchor to the code it describes. This is the RIGHT place — a doc is code-ANCHORED,\n    drift-TRACKED (the freshness sweep) and AUTO-HEALED (the doc-steward); a mem0 vector cannot\n    be anchored/swept/auto-rewritten, so how-it-works left only in mem0 silently rots. Do NOT\n    park a runbook in mem0.\n  - **WHY a subsystem/decision is the way it is** (the rationale behind a design, not how it works):\n    READ via `rationale:feed { topic }` — a topic-keyed projection over the relevant\n    plan-decisions + work-items + insights, kept fresh by the event engine (`topics:list` for the\n    topic, then `plans:get`/`docs:get` on an entry's `ref` for the full text). No FK — coord_event_log outlives this table's retention.\"},{\"name\":\"assumption_set_id\",\"type\":\"bigint\",\"nullable\":true,\"default\":null,\"comment\":\"P-009/D-011: WATERMARK over harness_shared.agent_facts.id — the caller's live assumption set is every non-retracted, non-superseded kind='assumption' fact of theirs with id <= this value. NULL = no assumptions declared.\"},{\"name\":\"goal_ref\",\"type\":\"text\",\"nullable\":true,\"default\":null,\"comment\":\"P-009/D-011: the RESOLVED goal ref this call served (e.g. 'WI-6393', 'plan:slug#P-009'), auto-derived from the caller's claimed work-item / plan-item. NULL = unreadable, or row predates migration 1043.\"},{\"name\":\"serving_build_sha\",\"type\":\"text\",\"nullable\":true,\"default\":null,\"comment\":\"WHAT CODE that process had LOADED: short git sha, resolved once at boot. NULL = no assumptions declared.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"goal_ref\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"P-009/D-011: the RESOLVED goal ref this call served (e.g. 'WI-6393', 'plan:slug#P-009'), auto-derived from the caller's claimed work-item / plan-item. NULL = no goal claimed.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"call_origin\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"Who CHOSE this call: agent (the model) | hook (per-turn harness automation) | ui | system | unknown. NULL = row predates migration 809. See lib/telemetry-call-origin.ts.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"call_origin_source\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"How call_origin was determined: declared (caller marked itself, e.g. &origin=hook on the MCP url) | derived (inferred from request shape). Filter on declared for certainty.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"serving_host\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"WHICH SERVICE served this call: the host label 'port-<n>' (else 'pid-<n>' when no port is resolvable), stable across restarts of the same logical service. Same vocabulary as stale-routine-executor's condition keys, so pages and calls join. NULL = row predates migration 1043. See lib/serving-host-identity.ts.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"serving_process_id\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"WHICH RUN of that service: kernel-backed per-process identity 'linux:<boot-id>:<start-ticks>', immune to the ~daily PID reuse on this box. Process boot time needs no column — it is min(invoked_at) GROUP BY this. NULL = unreadable, or row predates migration 1043.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"serving_build_sha\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"WHAT CODE that process had LOADED: short git sha, resolved once at boot. NULL means the row predates migration 1043 OR the process could not PROVE its loaded bytes (bundled artifact with no baked sha) — it is never the current checkout's HEAD standing in for an unknown. Compare against tree HEAD to compute absolute code age; this is what makes host staleness measurable from the LEDGER, without cooperation from the stale process.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"goal_id\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"WI-1742833: semantic goal served by the caller, resolved at telemetry write time from GOAL mode then inherited session brief; nullable when unscoped.\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"goal_actor_class\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"nullable\\\":true,\\\"default\\\":null,\\\"comment\\\":\\\"WI-1742833: write-time actor class: holder-agent, drain-fleet-member, or goal-descendant-agent; nullable when goal_id is NULL.\\\"}],\\\"indexes\\\":[{\\\"name\\\":\\\"tool_invocations_activity_adv_session_lookup_idx\\\",\\\"definition\\\":\\\"CREATE INDEX tool_invocations_activity_adv_session_lookup_idx ON harness_shared.tool_invocations USING btree (workspace_id, ((args_json ->> 'adv_session_id'::text)), invoked_at DESC, id DESC) WHERE ((tool_name = ANY (ARRAY['activity:report'::text, 'activity_report'::text])) AND (args_json ? An unmeasured or stale\n   * pool may still be a dead endpoint, so those deadlines stay non-retryable.\n   */\n  readonly retryable: boolean;\n  /** Bounded local view of active tickets captured before the timed-out ticket is released. */\n  readonly acquisitionTickets: AcquireTicketSnapshot | null;\n  constructor(label: string, deadlineMs: number, elapsedMs: number, pool?: string) {\n    const acquisitionTickets = pool ? acquireTicketSnapshot(pool) : null;\n    const measured = pool ? describeAcquirePressure(pool) : null;\n    // A decisive measurement has already answered \"which cause\"; re-printing the\n    // cause fork after it would bury the answer under the procedure it replaces.\n    const tail = measured?.decisive\n      ? ACQUIRE_QUEUE_LOCATION_RESIDUAL\n      : `Two causes present identically at this point — (a) the pool's resolved endpoint is ` +\n        `unreachable and postgres.js is silently retrying its INITIAL connect forever without ` +\n        `rejecting (WI-7097), or (b) the CLIENT pool's acquire queue is saturated while the ` +\n        `server is perfectly healthy. Server capacity does NOT decide (b), so ` +\n        `dev:service_health / pg_stat_activity looking fine is not evidence against it — ` +\n        `check this process's own pcusp:${pool ?? '<pool>'}:p<pid> rows and ` +\n        `PAPERCUSP_DB_POOL_MAX before the endpoint (WI-7097).`;\n    super(\n      // Stamped with the emitting BUILD — see build-stamp.ts (EI-19484133375867605).\n      `${stampedTag('db-call-deadline')} \"${label}\" did not resolve within ${deadlineMs}ms ` +\n        `(waited ${elapsedMs}ms). ` +\n        (measured\n          ? `${measured.text} `\n          : `No acquire measurements were available for this call, so both causes are still open. `) +\n        tail,\n    );\n    this.name = 'DbCallDeadlineError';\n    this.label = label;\n    this.deadlineMs = deadlineMs;\n    this.elapsedMs = elapsedMs;\n    this.pool = pool ?? null;\n    this.measured = measured?.text ?? null;\n    this.retryable = measured?.decisive === true;\n    this.acquisitionTickets = acquisitionTickets;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Options for the narrow pre-handler retry used by dispatch seams. */\nexport interface RetryOnRetryableDbDeadlineOptions {\n  /** Additional attempts after the first. Defaults to two. */\n  retries?: number;\n  /** Linear backoff base in milliseconds. Defaults to 150ms. */\n  backoffMs?: number;\n  /** Injectable sleep for deterministic tests. */\n  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;\n  /** Optional observability hook before each retry. */\n  onRetry?: (attempt: number, error: DbCallDeadlineError) => void;\n}\n\nconst defaultDbDeadlineRetrySleep = (ms: number): Promise<void> =>\n  new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));\n"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12308-19a2-7631-a242-ca75f623c446","create_time":1791589514.2398975}},"metadata":{"client_authored":false,"fallback_token_limit_override":12000}}

The hang this guards against happens strictly earlier: against a dead\n * endpoint, postgres-js's `closed()` special-cases a pool's FIRST connection\n * attempt and calls `reconnect()` with exponential backoff FOREVER without ever\n * invoking `error()`/`queryError()` — so the caller's query is never rejected\n * and the call blocks at `sql.begin()` BEFORE its handler runs. That is what\n * took 100% of MCP dispatch down on 2026-08-03 (including `coord:whoami`) while\n * `/api/health` stayed at 2ms on the unaffected ADMIN pool; only a process\n * restart cleared it.\n *\n * `run` receives:\n *  - `disarm()`  — call once the caller's own work is about to begin.\n *  - `expired()` — true if the deadline already fired. CHECK THIS before\n *    invoking the caller's callback and throw if set: `Promise.race` does not\n *    cancel the losing promise, so without the check a timed-out transaction\n *    would still run the handler with nobody awaiting its result. Throwing\n *    inside the `sql.begin` callback rolls the transaction back instead.\n *\n * `opts.pool` is the `buildClient` label of the pool being acquired from\n * (`org-app` / `org-admin`). Passing it registers this acquisition in the\n * acquire registry, which is what lets a breach report MEASURED waiting/held\n * counts instead of the manual 3-step probe — see `acquire-registry.ts`. It is\n * optional so a caller with no single identifiable pool still gets the guard.\n */\nexport function withAcquisitionDeadline<T>(\n  run: (phase: { disarm: () => void; expired: () => boolean }) => Promise<T>,\n  opts: { ms?: number; label: string; pool?: string },\n): Promise<T> {\n  const ms = opts.ms ?? DEFAULT_TX_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_MS;\n  const startedAt = Date.now();\n  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;\n  let settled = false;\n  let expired = false;\n  // Registered BEFORE the first await so this caller counts itself among the\n  // waiters its own error reports — \"18 waiting, oldest 44.9s\" includes you.\n  const ticket = opts.pool ? beginAcquire(opts.pool) : null;\n  const clearDeadlineTimer = () => {\n    settled = true;\n    if (timer) {\n      clearTimeout(timer);\n      timer = undefined;\n    }\n  };\n  // What `run` receives: the connection is in hand and the caller's own work is\n  // about to begin, so stop the clock AND move this ticket waiting -> held.\n  const disarm = () => {\n    clearDeadlineTimer();\n    ticket?.acquired();\n  };\n  const deadline = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {\n    timer = setTimeout(() => {\n      if (settled) return;\n      expired = true;\n      settled = true;\n      // Constructed while this ticket is still WAITING, on purpose: the snapshot\n      // in the message is the state at the moment of the breach.\n      reject(new DbCallDeadlineError(opts.label, ms, Date.now() - startedAt, opts.pool));\n    }, ms);\n    // Never hold the process open on this timer alone.\n    timer.unref?.();\n  });\n  let work: Promise<T>;\n  try {\n    work = Promise.resolve(run({ disarm, expired: () => expired }));\n  } catch (error) {\n    clearDeadlineTimer();\n    ticket?.release();\n    return Promise.reject(error);\n  }\n  return Promise.race([work, deadline]).finally(() => {\n    clearDeadlineTimer();\n    // Must run on EVERY exit path — a ticket that is never released leaks a\n    // waiter and inflates every later snapshot, which would make this\n    // diagnostic worse than none.\n    ticket?.release();\n  });\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":34186}},"started_at_ms":1791589522626,"completed_at_ms":1791589522627}}

`${(ms / 1_000).toFixed(1)}s` : `${ms}ms`;\n}\n\n/**\n * What the counters concluded.\n *\n * `client-saturation` and `queued` both RULE OUT a dead endpoint, so they are\n * `decisive` — the caller should print a short \"where is the queue\" residual\n * instead of the full dead-endpoint-vs-saturation procedure. `never-acquired`\n * and `stale-success` leave the fork open, so the full procedure still applies.\n */\nexport type AcquireVerdict = 'never-acquired' | 'stale-success' | 'queued' | 'client-saturation';\n\nexport interface AcquirePressureReport {\n  /** Numbers first, then the ONE conclusion they license, then their honest bound. */\n  text: string;\n  verdict: AcquireVerdict;\n  /** True when the measurement settles the dead-endpoint-vs-saturation fork by itself. */\n  decisive: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * The measured lead for a deadline error.\n *\n * Returns null when nothing was measured for `pool` (no ticket has ever been\n * opened and the pool was never built here) — the caller then falls back to the\n * manual discriminator, rather than printing a row of confident zeroes.\n */\nexport function describeAcquirePressure(pool: string): AcquirePressureReport | null {\n  const s = acquireSnapshot(pool);\n  if (s.max === null && s.totalAcquired === 0 && s.waiting === 0 && s.held === 0) return null;\n\n  const counts =\n    `MEASURED IN THIS PROCESS (pid ${process.pid}), pool \"${s.pool}\": ` +\n    `${s.waiting} acquisition(s) WAITING (oldest ${fmtAge(s.oldestWaitMs)}), ` +\n    `${s.held} HELD at this seam (oldest ${fmtAge(s.oldestHeldMs)}), ` +\n    `pool max ${s.max ?? 'unknown'}; last successful acquisition on this pool ` +\n    `${s.lastAcquiredAgoMs === null ? 'NEVER' : `${fmtAge(s.lastAcquiredAgoMs)} ago`} ` +\n    `(${s.totalAcquired} total this process).`;\n\n  let verdict: AcquireVerdict;\n  let conclusion: string;\n  if (s.totalAcquired === 0) {\n    verdict = 'never-acquired';\n    conclusion =\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"== pg-deadline =="},{"type":"input_text","text":" * with it would also bound the caller's handler and kill legitimately long\n * tools. The hang this guards against happens strictly earlier: against a dead\n * endpoint, postgres-js's `closed()` special-cases a pool's FIRST connection\n * attempt and calls `reconnect()` with exponential backoff FOREVER without ever\n * invoking `error()`/`queryError()` — so the caller's query is never rejected\n * and the call blocks at `sql.begin()` BEFORE its handler runs. That is what\n * took 100% of MCP dispatch down on 2026-08-03 (including `coord:whoami`) while\n * `/api/health` stayed at 2ms on the unaffected ADMIN pool; only a process\n * restart cleared it.\n *\n * `run` receives:\n *  - `disarm()`  — call once the caller's own work is about to begin.\n *  - `expired()` — true if the deadline already fired. CHECK THIS before\n *    invoking the caller's callback and throw if set: `Promise.race` does not\n *    cancel the losing promise, so without the check a timed-out transaction\n *    would still run the handler with nobody awaiting its result. Throwing\n *    inside the `sql.begin` callback rolls the transaction back instead.\n *\n * `opts.pool` is the `buildClient` label of the pool being acquired from\n * (`org-app` / `org-admin`). Passing it registers this acquisition in the\n * acquire registry, which is what lets a breach report MEASURED waiting/held\n * counts instead of the manual 3-step probe — see `acquire-registry.ts`. It is\n * optional so a caller with no single identifiable pool still gets the guard.\n */\nexport function withAcquisitionDeadline<T>(\n  run: (phase: { disarm: () => void; expired: () => boolean }) => Promise<T>,\n  opts: { ms?: number; label: string; pool?: string },\n): Promise<T> {\n  const ms = opts.ms ?? DEFAULT_TX_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_MS;\n  const startedAt = Date.now();\n  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;\n  let settled = false;\n  let expired = false;\n  // Registered BEFORE the first await so this caller counts itself among the\n  // waiters its own error reports — \"18 waiting, oldest 44.9s\" includes you.\n  const ticket = opts.pool ? beginAcquire(opts.pool) : null;\n  const clearDeadlineTimer = () => {\n    settled = true;\n    if (timer) {\n      clearTimeout(timer);\n      timer = undefined;\n    }\n  };\n  // What `run` receives: the connection is in hand and the caller's own work is\n  // about to begin, so stop the clock AND move this ticket waiting -> held.\n  const disarm = () => {\n    clearDeadlineTimer();\n    ticket?.acquired();\n  };\n  const deadline = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {\n    timer = setTimeout(() => {\n      if (settled) return;\n      expired = true;\n      settled = true;\n      // Constructed while this ticket is still WAITING, on purpose: the snapshot\n      // in the message is the state at the moment of the breach.\n      reject(new DbCallDeadlineError(opts.label, ms, Date.now() - startedAt, opts.pool));\n    }, ms);\n    // Never hold the process open on this timer alone.\n    timer.unref?.();\n  });\n  let work: Promise<T>;\n  try {\n    work = Promise.resolve(run({ disarm, expired: () => expired }));\n  } catch (error) {\n    clearDeadlineTimer();\n    ticket?.release();\n    return Promise.reject(error);\n  }\n  return Promise.race([work, deadline]).finally(() => {\n    clearDeadlineTimer();\n    // Must run on EVERY exit path — a ticket that is never released leaks a\n    // waiter and inflates every later snapshot, which would make this\n    // diagnostic worse than none.\n    ticket?.release();\n  });\n"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12308-19a2-7631-a242-ca75f623c446","create_time":1791589523.851696}},"metadata":{"client_authored":false,"fallback_token_limit_override":12000}}
